text:
asha: Heads-up: I ran a microbench with simulated region flaps and found a surprising interaction between client hedged-writes and our active-active primary assertion. TL;DR hedged-writes can create dual-success acknowledgements when the primary flips mid-flight.

tyler: Can you give the short sequence? is this the client sending parallel requests to two regions?

asha: Yup. Client hedges to reduce tail latency: sends write to primary X and to fallback Y after 50ms. If primary flips to Y during that 50ms window, both routes may succeed and both replicas accept, then our cross-region reconciliation finds no conflict but GH-ownership asserts different owners for audit.

noor: So we end up with two accepted writes that look equivalent but violate the single-owner invariant we promise to customers with residency constraints. Do we surface this as a conflict?

pav: Also, our current owner-assertion runs at the final KV commit, not at the proxy. So a write can be accepted locally before owner-check completes. That matches other threads but is a big problem when clients hedge.

asha: Ideas we've discussed: 1) server-side hedging aware of owner hints (don't hedge if owner_hint != proxy_region) 2) require proxy owner-assertion synchronously for hedged writes 3) client-side opt-out for hedging when tenant residency is strict.

tyler: Synchronous owner assert increases latency but only for hedged flows (rare). Might be acceptable if we keep it gated by tenant flag. Also we could have proxy return a "fast-reject" header so client knows to stop hedging.

noor: I like a hybrid: add a new header X-Res-Mode: strict|relaxed. Client sets it (SDKs default based on tenant metadata). Proxy honors it: in strict => reject hedged/fanout attempts; in relaxed => allow hedging but tag writes.

pav: Tagging is important. If a hedged write wins in a non-resident region, we should attach immutable provenance: owner_at_commit, routed_from, client_hedged=true, sweep_required=true. That helps audits.

compliance-bot: compliance: tenants with GDPR/DSR flags require server-side strict residency enforcement. Fail-open hedging is disallowed.

asha: Then we need a clear failure mode: if proxy refuses hedged write, return 409 + Retry-After maybe with region hint. SDK can automatically retry to resident region.

tyler: Another option: lightweight quorum for hedged writes: require a fast ack from the declared owner before accepting secondary's success. That makes secondaries optimistic but not final. Complexity to implement but keeps client latency low.

noor: Quorum implies cross-region round-trip in failure cases which defeats hedging. Maybe only used for strict tenants.

pav: Implementation notes: - extend tenancy metadata with hedging_policy: strict|allow-tagged|client-only - proxy checks header/tenancy metadata - telemetry: hedged_write_attempts, hedged_write_blocked, hedged_write_conflicts - audit log export for tagged writes

asha: Deploy-bot: staging proxy v2 has initial header plumbing (deployed at 1769301300) :white_check_mark:

tyler: Tests to add: chaos test where client hedges + control-plane owner flip; assert no untagged cross-region commits for strict tenants. Also SDK test: auto-disable hedging if 409+Retry-After received.

noor: Edge-case: what if a client hedges because they never received the region hint (mobile offline)? SDK may not know tenant strictness. We should have server-side defaults (opt to strict for tenant if residency flag present).

pav: Agree. Also add a cache in proxies for tenant hedging_policy with short TTL and invalidation on owner-change events. That avoids per-request control-plane reads.

asha: Action items: 1) Add hedging_policy to tenancy API (owner: pav) 2) Proxy: honor X-Res-Mode header, block/annotate hedged writes (owner: tyler) 3) SDK: wire auto-retry behavior on 409+Retry-After (owner: noor) 4) Telemetry + audit export (owner: asha).

tyler: One more thing: metrics should include percent of client-visible 409s for strict tenants. Product needs to know UX impact.

noor: I'll add synthetic run for mobile offline case where SDK can't set header: ensure proxy enforces tenant default.

pav: Sounds good. I'll draft a short RFC describing hedging_policy states and expected semantics, include sequence diagrams.

asha: Thanks all. I'll open the telemetry tickets and link the RFC when ready.

deploy-bot: canary test started against staging cluster 1769301350 :gear:

tyler: No objections. moving to implement.
